findings.title: V2 canManage() grants manage on all groups to admins that only have the VIEW scope
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, i.e. when the caller merely has the 'view' scope on the all-groups ('Groups') resource. canManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() enforces via auth.groups().requireManage(), so an admin granted only read access to all groups can create new top-level groups. This looks like a copy/paste of canView(); the interface javadoc in GroupPermissionEvaluator (lines 75-76) even documents 'VIEW or MANAGE' for canManage(), which is the wrong contract. It should check only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE (mirroring canManage(GroupModel) on line 79). No test covers the negative case (VIEW-all must not allow creation).

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In the findByType callback, hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) looks the resource up again by name using the resource's ID (hasPermission does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)), which never matches because V2 group resources are named by group ID. The lookup therefore always falls back to the all-groups resource, and when that has a VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission the code adds groupResource.getId() (an authz resource UUID, not a group ID) to the returned set. UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource put this set into session attribute UserModel.GROUPS, which the user store uses to filter the DB query by group membership. Consequences: with per-group permissions the set is effectively always empty, so paging (first/max) is applied before the in-memory canView filter and pages come back short or empty; with an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission the set contains a bogus ID so the user search returns nothing at all. Both calls should use groupResource.getName() (the group ID), as the V1 implementation does with resource.getName().substring(...).

findings.title: NPE when the Groups resource-type resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() returns null when supportsAuthorizationSchema() is false (feature disabled, realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled() false, or session.getContext().getRealm() differs from the realm whose admin-permissions client was resolved by root.realmResourceServer()). hasPermission() then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, null) and resource.getScopes() without a null check, producing a NullPointerException (500) instead of a deny. This is reachable e.g. for a realm whose admin-permissions client still exists after the flag has been turned off. A null check returning false is needed.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong predicate
findings.body: The javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says it throws when canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but the implementations (GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers) check canManageMembers(GroupModel). manage-membership and manage-members are distinct scopes with different semantics, so the documentation is misleading. Additionally, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()'s @return says 'Stream of IDs' although it returns a Set.

findings.title: getResourceName() not extended for the new Groups resource type
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases only USERS (mapping the all-resource to 'All users' and per-user resources to the username). For the newly added GROUPS resource type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is never set for schema-created group resources (getOrCreateResource creates them with the group ID as name and no display name), so permission listings for group resources will show null/raw UUIDs instead of 'All groups'/the group name or path. The Groups branch (and a 'group not found' check analogous to the user one) should be added.

findings.title: Global view short-circuit removed; policy evaluation now runs per group in listings
findings.body: The previous code computed canViewGlobal once and only called canView(g) per element when it was false. Now stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView) (and the same change in GroupResource.getSubGroups line 179) evaluates per group. For admins whose access comes from an all-groups permission rather than a realm role, every listed group triggers resourceStore.findByName, a fallback lookup of the resource-type resource, policyStore.findByResource and a full policy evaluation. Listing large group trees under FGAP V2 will be noticeably slower than before. Keeping a single canView() check before the per-group filter would avoid this.

findings.title: switch on resourceType throws NullPointerException for null input
findings.body: The new switch (resourceType) statement dereferences the string. Before this change a null resourceType resulted in name == null and the explicit IllegalStateException 'Could not map resource object...'; now a null value yields a bare NullPointerException. Callers that reach getOrCreateResource for non-scope policy types without a resource type would surface a 500 with an unhelpful message. Guard for null before the switch or include it in the default message.

findings.title: No coverage for VIEW-all not granting manage, for DB-level group filtering, or for group members endpoint
findings.body: After granting the all-groups VIEW permission, the test only asserts that groups are listed; it never asserts that creating a top-level group is still forbidden, which would have caught canManage() accepting the VIEW scope. There is also no test exercising user search with first/max paging or with an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission, which would expose getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returning resource IDs instead of group IDs, and no test of GET /groups/{id}/members (requireViewMembers) under VIEW_MEMBERS / MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions.
